messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 PagerDuty: spike in 5xx and stream disconnects for /v1/generate in az-east1a. 30% error for the last 3m. Severity: p1.
jamie-oncall: I'm on it, grabbing logs and splitting traffic. starting failover play.
lee-sre: seeing NIC tx errors on a subset of hosts, kernel drops + retransmits. looks like a host-level network wave.
maya-rt: traffic graph -> p95 latency up 2.1x, error rate concentrated for inference fleet in az-east1a, model p50 fine.
jamie-oncall: immediate mitigation: shift 40% of traffic off az-east1a to us-west-2, enable model fallback to redwood-lite-quant for lower mem footprint. applying routing change now.
ops-bot: runbook step executed: route-policy set -> region-weight-adjust {az-east1a: 60, us-west-2: 40}.
lee-sre: confirming: I see fewer retransmits on the hosts we evacuated. but some remaining hosts still flapping.
marta-cust: @jamie any customer impact so we can notify support?
jamie-oncall: yes — spike affected short-lived streaming sessions and some sync generate calls. estimated 3% of active customers hit higher latency or 5xx. flagging support-sla.
maya-rt: starting KV-cache regen on failover targets to avoid cold-cache penalties. running small-batch populate.
lee-sre: I opened a ticket with cloud provider, they report "host network corridor" events in az-east1a affecting multicast/tx path. they're doing host replacements.
jamie-oncall: switching to oncall handoff: @lee-sre will lead remediation, I'll coordinate customer comms. paging rotation -> handoff to lee in 15m.
lee-sre: plan: cordon and drain the 8 impacted ephemeral hosts, reattach to alternate AZ if available; otherwise keep traffic steered. executing drain now: `kubectl drain gpu-ephemeral-045 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
ops-bot: drain completed on 6/8 hosts; two failing drain due to stuck GPU driver process.
lee-sre: killing stuck driver process, retry drain. also expanding route shift to 50% to reduce risk while provider replaces hosts.
jamie-oncall: noted. I'll draft a brief status update for affected customers: short blip, partial traffic shift, engineering working with cloud provider, ETA next update in 30m.
marta-cust: thanks — I'll prep support thread and include suggested mitigation (retry client backoff).
maya-rt: monitoring: errors dropped to 2% after route change; p95 latency trending down but still 1.3x baseline for a subset of requests.
lee-sre: provider confirms 6 hosts replaced, NIC firmware applied. continuing validation.
jamie-oncall: oncall handoff complete. I'm switching status to monitoring. @ops-bot, please keep a live log of routing weight changes in thread.
ops-bot: noted. route-policy now {az-east1a:50, us-west-2:50}. logged at ts 8151112330.
lee-sre: full drain succeeded and new hosts healthy. I will keep routing at 50/50 for 20m then slowly return to normal if metrics stable.
maya-rt: scheduling regression eval for traffic that used the quant fallback to ensure output quality acceptable. posting eval results in 45m.
jamie-oncall: thanks team. postmortem pre-label: single-AZ host-network wave -> traffic steer + host replacement mitigated impact; follow-ups: add automated eviction for stuck GPU driver processes, improve cross-AZ warmup for KV caches.
marta-cust: support notified customers in affected cohort. no major SLA breaches. closing customer comm loop after postmortem. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident transitioned to monitoring. Final note: keep thread open until metrics at baseline for 1h.
